# Executive summary

Instructors and learners choosing an R tutorial often have to inspect its repository to find prerequisites and evidence that the exercises still work. Descriptions differ across formats and may leave maintenance status unclear.

**tutorialverse will help instructors and learners find R tutorials suited to their needs and see the reported prerequisites, check results, and review status.** Authors will describe tutorials with shared metadata. An R package will use adapters to run supported checks through existing engines and produce common reports. A searchable registry will combine descriptions, reports, and human reviews, linking readers to original lessons. Community review and scheduled checks will help keep entries current.

An [initial prototype](https://github.com/tutorial-verse/tutorialverse/tree/feat/engine-adapters-and-checks) already demonstrates the proposed adapter model across all three engines. Grant work will extend this foundation to curated registry records, CI-based validation, author-effort measurement, and community-reviewed metadata.

Over 12 months, we will harden and extend support for learnr, learnr2, and Quarto Live, index 5–10 existing tutorials, and use four small examples to test the adapters across teaching contexts. Carpentries-style materials will also be indexed, with stated limits on automated checks. Existing tools will provide browser execution and static hosting. We request USD 10,000 for this work.
